title: Preserve a catalytic time floor to defeat correlated early shutdown
statement: For four-arm independent retained grafts with symmetric old/new access and eta>0, fixed k,d>0, T~Exp(d), q(T)=1-exp(-k*T) and Poisson(N) independent candidates conditional on T, zero-weld failure F_N=E[exp(-N*P4(q(T)))]. Jensen gives F_N>=exp(-N*E[P4]). As N->infinity at fixed parameters, F_N~d*sqrt(pi)/(2*eta*k*sqrt(3*N)). If catalytic access truly lasts T+T0 with guaranteed T0>0, F_N<=exp(-N*P4(1-exp(-k*T0))).

requires: Exactly the declared four-arm two-hit independent-graft model with old/new fraction theta=1/2, conditional independence given one common T, Poisson candidate mean N, eta>0 and fixed k,d>0.
For the improved bound, a deterministic positive catalytic period with all actual reaction prerequisites retained, not just a longer expected access time.

assumptions: Independent per-candidate windows and a common regional window are different interfaces. The N^-1/2 tail is fixed-parameter asymptotic, not a finite-N calibrated estimate.
Single-hit/preanchored or otherwise changed mechanisms require their own short-time law. Real correlated regions need separate analysis.
costs: Extra linker abundance pays N supply; guaranteed T0 pays actual enzyme/reactant/water/contact retention and duration. Physical calibration and donor harm are not supplied by the asymptotic.
contract.units: k,d are inverse time, T,T0 are time, N is a mean candidate count and eta and failure are dimensionless.
contract.obstruction: Measure the actual joint access/reaction/retention process before importing the shared-clock reliability law.

body: Here P4(q)=1-2*(1-eta*q/2)^4+(1-eta*q)^4. Conditional Poisson thinning gives the zero-weld expression. Its small-time expansion is P4(q(t))=3*(eta*k*t)^2+O(t^3). Scale t by N^(-1/2) in the exponential-clock integral; positive times bounded away from zero contribute exponentially little, leaving the Gaussian half-integral and stated constant. A deterministic time floor makes P4 uniformly positive, giving the exponential upper bound. Retaining a catalyst alone does not guarantee active enzyme, acceptors, water or molecular contact throughout T0. These are model-conditional laws, not calibrated repair reliability or an all-mechanism two-hit lower bound.
